analysis:
The supplied units are head-side text of docs/developer/test.md. The patch adds a documentation-only section, 'Cluster Pair Coordinated Update', around head lines 1043-1085. That range lies beyond the excerpts supplied in these units, which end at line 920. The patch excerpt is truncated at its end and names unit tests for pair-coordinated updates, the update start check and candidate rollback. I examined the visible portions for security-relevant statements. The visible text has no commands that touch production, no secrets, and no instructions to disable controls. Fixtures use isolated temporary directories and synthetic credentials. The text repeatedly states that the tests do not establish hardware, Apple or platform qualification.

Because this is a docs-only change, it adds no code attack surface and no regression against T-041, TB-011, T-053, T-059/TB-012 or T-043 (watchdog rollback). Retained claims about add-on hold, logout, endpoint resumption and SSD cache testing stay consistent with the threat model. The test docs use DARKBLOOM_SSD_TEST_TMPDIR, which they say is test-only, and tell users never to use production cache roots or keys.

Limits: the Cluster Pair update section (lines 1043+) and the new tests' behaviour are not in the supplied text. The real updater, rollback and start-check code, which touch T-043 and the signed-artifact trust, are outside this batch. If code accompanies this PR, a deeper pass should check pair-update coordination, partner-asked trust, and the rollback authority. I make no claim about those from the docs alone.
